metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Morocco

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Morocco using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, so analyses in the PISA database are typically conducted with sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For users reproducing these estimates, the OECD PISA database guidance should be followed to apply the provided student sampling weights and to use the recommended variance estimation approach for confidence intervals.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the provided document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking proficiency and related subgroup comparisons, rather than an analysis that explicitly models PV-based achievement with a documented PV-combining procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet text because it does not describe any student-level analytic dataset construction or imputation/deletion rules; those details are typically contained in the main PISA technical documentation and database methodology rather than in country factsheets.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The Morocco factsheet reports results for students in Morocco who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science and for whom the creative thinking assessment was administered as part of PISA 2022 Volume III. The text specifies that 6,867 students in 178 schools completed the assessment in Morocco (representing about 455,000 15-year-olds), but it does not provide additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., missingness thresholds or item/task completion criteria) beyond this completion statement.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Morocco’s performance on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test administered to 15-year-olds in 2022. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Morocco’s mean creative thinking score is 15 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly below the OECD average (33). Only 23% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), while 5% are top performers at Levels 5–6. The factsheet also reports within-Morocco performance gaps by socioeconomic quartiles and gender, and it describes how creative thinking relates to mathematics and reading performance (including the share of variance uniquely explained by mathematics). Because this is a descriptive factsheet rather than an ML study, no predictive modeling pipeline, PV-combining method, or missing-data procedure is documented in the provided text.
